workItem.title: Selective version control for .praxis workflow state

requirements.statement: Workflow state must be safe and useful to commit: the authoritative per-work-item state is portable across machines and contains no secrets, while everything private, transient or per-operator stays out of version control, with exactly one authoritative copy of each work item.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Persisted service localPath is stored relative to the workflow repository and resolved to an absolute path on load, so no machine path or username is committed; existing absolute values keep working.
index.json is a rebuildable cache: if it is missing but items/ exists, it is rebuilt from the items; a single item becomes current, several require explicit selection and never guess.

A documented .gitignore block excludes approvals, ledgers, keys, locks, temp and stale files, the per-operator index and the legacy/tombstone state.json, and tracks items/*.json and .praxis/quality checks and proposals.
Migration and rebuild never create a second authoritative copy of a work item.
A scan of every tracked-eligible file under .praxis finds no credential, token, private key or absolute home path.
The repositories in this workspace adopt the policy and commit their work items.

openQuestions: Should the index be tracked? Proposed: no, it carries per-operator selection and timestamps, and is rebuildable.

nextActions: workflow-store: portable localPath, index rebuild, WORK_ITEM_SELECTION_REQUIRED
Adopt in workspace repos after migration

decisions.statement: Tracked: .praxis/workflow/items/*.json (authoritative WorkflowState per work item: requirements, stories, decisions, handoffs, verdicts, coverage, changes, history) and .praxis/quality/** except logs (checks.json, adapter.mjs, proposals/). Ignored: .praxis/workflow/index.json (rebuildable cache holding per-operator current selection and timestamps), .praxis/workflow/state.json (legacy before migration, tombstone after; never a second authoritative copy), .praxis/workflow/.lock*, *.tmp, *.stale-*, .praxis/approvals/, any *.ledger, *.pem, *.key, .praxis/local/, .praxis/**/*.log. Store changes in workflow-store.ts: on write, services[].localPath inside or beside the workflow repository is persisted relative to the repository root (portable) and resolved to absolute on load; paths already absolute are read unchanged and are rewritten relative on the next write. Missing index.json with items/ present rebuilds the index from the items (updatedAt taken from the file mtime is NOT used; updatedAt is the rebuild time) and sets current only when exactly one item exists, otherwise current is null and commands without workItemId fail with WORK_ITEM_SELECTION_REQUIRED listing the ids. state.json stays a tombstone. Documentation: docs in praxis-runtime (PRAXIS-STATE-POLICY.md) with the exact .gitignore block. Adoption here: add the block to each repository .gitignore, migrate with the new runtime, run a secret/absolute-path scan, commit items.

implementationUnits.summary: praxis-runtime: services[].localPath persisted relative (toPortable/toAbsolute), index.json rebuilt from items/ with WORK_ITEM_SELECTION_REQUIRED instead of guessing, WORKFLOW_CONFLICT when state.json and items/ coexist. tools/scripts/praxis-state-policy.mjs adopt/scan (idempotent .gitignore block verified with git check-ignore; secret and home-path scanner reports kind and place only). PRAXIS-STATE-POLICY.md. Tests: state-policy.test.ts (7), praxis-state-policy.test.mjs (5); negative control: 6 of 7 fail on the previous store.

history.note: Owner decision: track durable team-relevant workflow artifacts (requirements, stories, decisions, handoffs, verification evidence, non-sensitive audit metadata) and exclude signing keys, credentials, private approval records, replay ledgers, temporary files, local session state and machine-specific configuration. Inspected reality: .praxis/workflow/state.json (legacy) or items/<id>.json hold the authoritative per-item WorkflowState; services[].localPath embeds absolute machine paths; index.json
